Playbook.name: AD — AS-REP Roasting: TGT Requested for a Pre-Auth-Disabled Account - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Credential Access / Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A TGT (4768) was requested for an account with Kerberos pre-authentication DISABLED (PreAuthType 0) - such AS-REP responses can be cracked offline. Triage question: which principal requested it, and is the target one of the known legacy no-preauth accounts or something new?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: An AS-REP-roastable account with a weak password hands the attacker an offline-crackable credential with zero failed-logon telemetry.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Signal.Name: No-preauth TGT
Signal.Details: 4768 where PreAuthType is 0 - only possible for accounts with DONT_REQ_PREAUTH set.

Input.name: $target_user
Input.description: Account whose TGT was requested without pre-auth.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Requesting client IP from the alert.

InitialAssessment.Rule: If the requesting source shows a wide sweep of MANY accounts, treat as roasting reconnaissance.
A single legacy application account requested from its own app server may be an accepted legacy configuration - verify, do not assume.

Investigation.Goal: Establish whether this was a targeted/sweeping roast attempt and whether the roastable account shows signs of subsequent use.

Step.name: Requesting source behavior - single account or sweep
Step.Purpose: Roasting tools enumerate; a sweep of 4768/4769 across accounts from the same source in minutes is attacker tradecraft.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE source.ip == "$source_ip" AND event.code IN ("4768","4769") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS req = COUNT(*), accounts = COUNT_DISTINCT(winlog.event_data.TargetUserName), enc = VALUES(winlog.event_data.TicketEncryptionType), preauth = VALUES(winlog.event_data.PreAuthType) BY event.code | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: accounts >> 1 in minutes, or RC4 (0x17) mixed in = enumeration/roast sweep. One request for one account = targeted or legacy app behavior.

Step.name: History of THIS account's no-preauth requests
Step.Purpose: Distinguish a routinely-requested legacy account from a first-time/rare request (new roast target).
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4768" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND winlog.event_data.PreAuthType == "0" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS req = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY src | SORT req DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: Multiple distinct requesting sources for a roastable account inside hours is abnormal; legacy apps request from a fixed server.

Step.name: Was the roastable account then USED (post-crack sign-in)
Step.Purpose: A successful logon for the roastable account from a new source after the request suggests the hash was cracked.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$target_user" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL src = COALESCE(TO_STRING(source.ip), "local") | STATS logons = COUNT(*), types = VALUES(winlog.event_data.LogonType), hosts = VALUES(host.name) BY src | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: Cracking usually takes longer than 4h - absence here does NOT clear the alert; presence from an unexpected source is a strong escalation signal.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the source sweeping many accounts (or RC4 service-ticket requests alongside), typical roasting tooling.
INV-03 shows the roastable account logging on from a source other than its historical requestor.
Node.Result: True Positive (Possible Cracked Credential - IR immediately)

Node.Condition: Single request; INV-02 shows the same fixed application server requesting this same account routinely; account is on the documented legacy no-preauth list.
Single request from a user workstation with no sweep and no documented legacy justification.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-ASREP-SWEEP, INV-02-ASREP-HISTORY, INV-03-ASREP-USE to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Genuinely approved security testing that requested AS-REP for audit purposes.

SOCAction.Item: Verify engagement scope; close as false_positive referencing the engagement.

TruePositive.Definition: Roasting activity: harvesting crackable AS-REP material, possibly followed by use of the cracked account.

Indicators.Item: Sweep across accounts from one source.
Requests for roastable accounts from sources that never requested them before.
Subsequent logon from a new source.

SOCAction.Item: Reset the roastable account password (long/random) and REMOVE DONT_REQ_PREAUTH.
Hunt the source's other Kerberos activity.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A legacy application account still configured without pre-auth, requested routinely by its application.

Indicators.Item: Fixed app-server source, regular cadence, same account for months.

SOCAction.Item: Register the account on the legacy no-preauth risk list with the owner.
Plan pre-auth enablement or migrate the app; meanwhile enforce a strong password.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Remove DONT_REQ_PREAUTH where the app allows.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Quarterly review of accounts with pre-auth disabled (should trend to zero).

QualityChecks.Check: Cracking happens offline - never close a sweep as benign because no success appeared within 4h.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Legacy dependency documented with owner sign-off; password strength verified.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account reset, pre-auth enabled or risk-accepted with expiry, source contained.
